- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days ahead.
- Model consistently underestimates the 10–30 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 1–3% bias upward for longer-term forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model fails to capture momentum; apply smoothing or lag correction to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5–7 days are below true outcome, assume “rebound bias” and increase forecast by 2–5% for days 8–15.
